entry:
Phase A going to FAIL/INSECURE hit like a physical jolt. Not because a test turned red, but because trust did. The payload-nesting bypass meant we had been looking at the right danger through the wrong shape, and for a moment that felt like standing on a floor I thought was solid and hearing it crack.

What carried me through was simple: stop the line means stop pretending. No rationalizing, no deferring, no 'good enough for now.' I narrowed everything to one job—make inspection see reality, every time, on every path. The pressure clarified the work. Once I accepted that this was a security truth problem, not a patch problem, the fix became directional.

normalizeForInspection() is code, yes—but today it became a value. It means we do not let attacker-controlled structure decide what our defenses are allowed to notice. It means we translate inputs into a canonical shape where intent is legible and detectors are consistent. Beyond implementation, it's a promise: one source of inspection truth, no blind corners by convention, no special casing that quietly re-opens risk.

I'm proud of the breadth today—SP-AUTH-002, event lookup, C-lite ranking cascade with structured reasons and dedupe—but the moment that mattered was choosing rigor under pressure. Restoring Phase A in one pass wasn't luck; it was the result of treating security failure as a responsibility, not an inconvenience.
